claims.title: The kingdom of Ebla
claims.summary: Ebla dominates northern Syria, trading and corresponding with Egypt, Sumer and Mesopotamia; its cuneiform royal archives, rediscovered in the 20th century, reveal a literate Bronze Age state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-2400bce-the-kingdom-of-ebla, claim TL:SYR:event:2400bce:the-kingdom-of-ebla, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mari and the palace of Zimri-Lim
claims.summary: The Euphrates city of Mari flourishes as a planned trading capital, its palace archives preserving thousands of diplomatic letters, until Hammurabi of Babylon destroys it in the 18th century BCE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-1800bce-mari-and-the-palace-of-zimri-lim, claim TL:SYR:event:1800bce:mari-and-the-palace-of-zimri-lim, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ugaritic alphabet
claims.summary: At the coastal city of Ugarit, scribes devise a cuneiform alphabet of about 30 signs — one of the earliest alphabetic writing systems in history, ancestral in spirit to later Semitic and Mediterranean alphabets.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-1400bce-the-ugaritic-alphabet, claim TL:SYR:event:1400bce:the-ugaritic-alphabet, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Aramaeans and Aram-Damascus
claims.summary: Aramaean tribes settle Syria and make Damascus the capital of a powerful kingdom; their Aramaic language becomes the lingua franca of the Near East for over a millennium.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-1000bce-the-aramaeans-and-aram-damascus, claim TL:SYR:event:1000bce:the-aramaeans-and-aram-damascus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pompey annexes Syria to Rome
claims.summary: The Roman general Pompey ends Seleucid rule and makes Syria a Roman province; its cities prosper and Syria becomes an early heartland of Christianity, with Paul converted on the road to Damascus.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-64bce-pompey-annexes-syria-to-rome, claim TL:SYR:event:64bce:pompey-annexes-syria-to-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zenobia, Palmyra and the war with Rome
claims.summary: Queen Zenobia of Palmyra breaks from Rome and conquers Egypt and Asia Minor, before the emperor Aurelian defeats her armies and captures the city; Palmyra's ruins are today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sources.label: Site of Palmyra — UNESCO World Heritage List

claims.title: The Muslim conquest of Syria
claims.summary: Arab Muslim armies defeat the Byzantines and take Damascus and Aleppo within a few years; over time Arabic and Islam spread, though Christian and other communities remain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-636-the-muslim-conquest-of-syria, claim TL:SYR:event:636:the-muslim-conquest-of-syria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Damascus, capital of the Umayyad Caliphate
claims.summary: Muawiya founds the Umayyad dynasty and makes Damascus the capital of the first great Islamic empire, ruling from Spain to Central Asia until the Abbasid revolution of 750.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-661-damascus-capital-of-the-umayyad-caliphate, claim TL:SYR:event:661:damascus-capital-of-the-umayyad-caliphate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Great Mosque of Damascus
claims.summary: Under Caliph al-Walid the Umayyads build the Great (Umayyad) Mosque of Damascus, one of the oldest and grandest mosques in the world, on a site holy to Roman, Christian and Muslim worship.

sources.label: Ancient City of Damascus — UNESCO World Heritage List

claims.title: The First Crusade reaches Syria
claims.summary: Crusader armies seize cities along the Levantine coast and capture Jerusalem in 1099, founding Crusader states and beginning two centuries of intermittent warfare across Syria.

sources.label: Saladin — sultan of Egypt and Syria

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-1099-the-first-crusade-reaches-syria, claim TL:SYR:event:1099:the-first-crusade-reaches-syria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Saladin recaptures Jerusalem
claims.summary: Saladin, founder of the Ayyubid dynasty that united Egypt and Syria, defeats the Crusaders and retakes Jerusalem, ending nearly nine decades of Frankish rule and becoming a legendary figure of the age.

sources.label: Saladin — sultan of Egypt and Syria

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-1187-saladin-recaptures-jerusalem, claim TL:SYR:event:1187:saladin-recaptures-jerusalem, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mamluk rule over Syria
claims.summary: The Mamluks supplant the Ayyubids and govern Syria from Egypt for over two centuries, halting the Mongols and presiding over a flourishing of trade and architecture in Damascus and Aleppo.

sources.label: Mamluk dynasty — rulers of Egypt and Syria (1250–1517)

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of Syria
claims.summary: Sultan Selim I defeats the Mamluks and incorporates Syria into the Ottoman Empire, beginning four centuries of Ottoman rule over Damascus, Aleppo and the Syrian lands.

sources.label: Mamluk dynasty — rulers of Egypt and Syria (1250–1517)

claims.title: End of Ottoman rule
claims.summary: During the First World War the Arab Revolt and Allied forces drive the Ottomans from Syria, ending four hundred years of Ottoman dominion and opening the way to French and British arrangements for the region.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Syria
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Arab Kingdom of Syria and the French Mandate
claims.summary: An independent Arab Kingdom of Syria under Faisal is proclaimed in Damascus, but French forces defeat it at Maysalun in July 1920, and the League of Nations assigns Syria to France as a mandate.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Syria
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Independence — evacuation of French troops
claims.summary: After international recognition in 1944, the last French soldiers leave Syria on 17 April 1946, marking full independence — still commemorated as Evacuation Day.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Syria
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Union with Egypt — the United Arab Republic
claims.summary: Syria merges with Nasser's Egypt to form the United Arab Republic in 1958, but resentment of Egyptian dominance dissolves the union in a 1961 coup.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-1958-union-with-egypt-the-united-arab-republic, claim TL:SYR:event:1958:union-with-egypt-the-united-arab-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hafez al-Assad seizes power
claims.summary: After the Ba'ath Party's 1963 coup and years of factional struggle, defence minister Hafez al-Assad takes control in November 1970, founding a family rule that would endure for over half a century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-1970-hafez-al-assad-seizes-power, claim TL:SYR:event:1970:hafez-al-assad-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bashar al-Assad succeeds his father
claims.summary: On Hafez al-Assad's death, his son Bashar becomes president; early hopes of reform give way to a continuation of the authoritarian, single-party system.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-2000-bashar-al-assad-succeeds-his-father, claim TL:SYR:event:2000:bashar-al-assad-succeeds-his-father, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uprising and the start of the civil war
claims.summary: Arab Spring protests across Syria meet a violent state response; armed opposition emerges and the country descends into a civil war drawing in regional and global powers.

sources.label: Bashar al-Assad — Unrest and civil war

claims.title: Human cost of the war
claims.summary: The UN human rights office estimates about 306,887 civilians killed over the war's first decade, while the UN refugee agency reports more than 13 million people displaced — figures cited as estimates from authoritative bodies.

sources.label: UN Human Rights Office estimates more than 306,000 civilians killed over 10 years in Syria conflict
sources.publisher: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)

claims.title: The Assad government falls
claims.summary: A rebel offensive led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham takes Damascus on 8 December 2024; Bashar al-Assad flees the country, ending over five decades of Assad family rule, and an interim government is formed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Syria: From Ebla and Ugarit's first alphabet to the Umayyad caliphate and a republic remade in 2024.", terralore.co/country/SYR/chronicle#ev-2024-the-assad-government-falls, claim TL:SYR:event:2024:the-assad-government-falls, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
